report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of graph_delta.py: mutation detection, specificity arm, and function-level delta helpers.
risks: line 565 | medium | `per_op` rows are keyed by `m.operator`; if `m.operator` is None or unhashable, `setdefault` raises TypeError, breaking the whole run. | Confirm the type of `m.operator` from the `generate` module.

line 587 | medium | `row["rate"]` divides by `row["n"]`; if `row["n"]` is 0, the guard returns 0.0, but the guard is redundant since `row["n"]` is incremented before the loop ends. | Verify no code path creates a row with n=0.

line 589 | high | `round(detected_total / len(mutants), 4)` divides by `len(mutants)`; if `mutants` is empty, this raises ZeroDivisionError, crashing the program. | Confirm the `generate` function never returns an empty list; otherwise add a guard.

line 603 | low | `_int_arg` silently falls back on malformed input, which is deliberate per docstring but could mask configuration errors in scripts. | Verify the report echoes the value as stated; if not, the docstring claim is broken.

line 627 | medium | `_git` uses a 60-second timeout; a slow repo or large diff could return None, causing `commit_shas` to treat the output as empty and silently report zero commits. | Confirm the timeout is sufficient for the intended repos; consider distinguishing timeout from real failure.

line 660 | high | `measure_commit` calls `_git(repo_root, "show", f"{sha}^:{rel}")`; if the commit is the root commit, `sha^` is invalid and `_git` returns None, causing `before` to be None and then treated as "added" (empty string), which may misclassify a deletion as an addition. | Verify the commit list excludes the root commit or handle the root case explicitly.

line 660 | high | `measure_commit` calls `_git(repo_root, "show", f"{sha}:{rel}")`; if the file is deleted in the commit, `git show` returns non-zero and `_git` returns None, so `after is None` and the file is skipped. This is correct. | No action needed; this is a handled case.

line 666 | medium | `_ast_refs(rel, before)` is called with `before` possibly None (root commit case), which may raise an unexpected exception if `_ast_refs` expects a string. | Confirm `_ast_refs` handles None or ensure `before` is never None.

line 670 | medium | `ty = len(_type_edge_keys(rel, after) ^ _type_edge_keys(rel, before))` uses set symmetric difference; if `_type_edge_keys` returns lists or non-set objects, the `^` operator may fail or behave unexpectedly. | Confirm `_type_edge_keys` returns sets.

line 680 | medium | `rec["pure_deletion"] = rec["added"] == 0 and rec["removed"] > 0`; this is the discriminator hypothesis, but it only counts refs, not type edges or structure, so a pure deletion that also changes type edges would still be counted as pure deletion. | Verify the hypothesis is intended to ignore type edges; if not, the rule may be too broad.

line 695 | medium | `specificity` returns `rows` which includes skipped rows? Actually `used = [r for r in rows if not r["skipped"] and r["per_file"]]`, so `rows` in the return is `used`, not all rows. This is fine but the key name `rows` is misleading; it's the used rows. | No action needed; just a naming clarity issue.

line 711 | high | `_refs_by_function` uses `out[f"{node.name}"] = out.get(node.name, Counter()) + c`; this merges counters by function name, but the docstring says "Qualify by line so two same-named methods in one file stay distinct." The code does NOT qualify by line; it merges by name, so two methods with the same name in the same file are combined, violating the docstring claim. | Confirm the docstring claim is intended; if so, this is a BROKEN claim.

line 711 | medium | `_refs_by_function` counts `ast.Name` and `ast.Attribute` nodes but does not count `ast.arg` (function arguments) or `ast.keyword` values; this may miss references that appear in default values or decorators. | Verify the intended scope of "references".

line 728 | low | `function_deltas` excludes functions added or removed wholesale, as documented, but it also excludes functions that exist in both but have no changes (added=0 and removed=0), which is correct. | No action needed.
todos: Confirm the type and hashability of `m.operator` in the `generate` module.
Confirm the `generate` function never returns an empty list; add a guard for zero mutants.
Verify the root-commit handling in `measure_commit` — decide whether to skip or treat as added.
Check whether `_type_edge_keys` returns sets; if not, adjust the symmetric difference.
Decide whether `_refs_by_function` should qualify by line as the docstring claims; if so, fix the key to include line numbers.
Verify the timeout in `_git` is sufficient for large repositories.

handoff.purpose: Mutation detection loop, specificity arm (real-commit measurement), and per-function delta helpers.

symbols.name: per_op
symbols.note: Local dict accumulating mutation detection results per operator.

symbols.name: detected_total
symbols.note: Local counter for total detected mutations.

symbols.name: _int_arg
symbols.note: Parses an integer flag from argv with silent fallback to default.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs a git command with a 60s timeout, returns stdout or None on error.

symbols.name: commit_shas
symbols.note: Returns non-merge commit SHAs touching Python files, newest first.

symbols.name: measure_commit
symbols.note: Measures layer deltas for one real commit, per-file and totals.

symbols.name: specificity
symbols.note: Runs the specificity arm over real commits and returns summary stats.

symbols.name: _refs_by_function
symbols.note: Parses a module and returns per-function reference multisets.

symbols.name: function_deltas
symbols.note: Returns rows for functions that exist in both versions and changed.

claims.text: "An unparsable half is not a detection and not a failure of the detector; counting it either way would move the headline for a bookkeeping reason."
claims.why: The try/except catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError and continues without counting.

claims.text: "``--limit 40``, or the default. Silent fallback is deliberate: a malformed limit should not lose the run, and the value is echoed in the written report either way."
claims.why: The code returns the default on malformed input, but the claim that the value is echoed in the report cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: "Non-merge commits touching Python, newest first. Merges are excluded because a merge's diff against its first parent attributes other people's work to it, which would pollute the corpus with changes it did not make."
claims.why: The git log command uses --no-merges and --format=%H with pathspec '*.py'; the result is split into lines.

claims.text: "A sweeping commit would dominate the distribution for a reason that has nothing to do with defectiveness. Bounded and SAID, never silently cut."
claims.why: The code checks len(files) > max_files and sets rec['skipped'] with the reason, returning early.
If `after` is None, the code continues, skipping the file.
If `before` is None, it is set to an empty string, treating the file as added.

claims.text: "unparseable at one end; not a finding"
claims.why: If `eb` or `ea` is truthy, the code continues, skipping the file.

claims.text: "Per-FUNCTION reference multisets. The granularity a defect actually has."
claims.why: The function parses the module and builds a Counter per function name.

claims.text: "Qualify by line so two same-named methods in one file stay distinct."
claims.why: The code uses `out[f"{node.name}"] = out.get(node.name, Counter()) + c`, which merges counters by name only; no line number is included in the key. Two methods with the same name in the same file would be combined, violating the claim.

claims.text: "One row per function that exists in BOTH versions and changed. Functions added or removed wholesale are excluded: a new function has no 'before' to lose references against, and counting it as a huge addition would swamp the distribution the rule is read from."
claims.why: The code intersects the function name sets and only appends rows when added or removed is non-zero.

observations.what: The mutation detection loop divides by `len(mutants)` without a zero-guard, risking ZeroDivisionError if the generator returns no mutants.
The `_refs_by_function` docstring claims line-qualification, but the code merges by function name only, violating the stated intent.
The root commit case in `measure_commit` is not handled; `sha^` may be invalid, causing `before` to be None and the file to be misclassified as added.
The `_git` function has a fixed 60-second timeout; if a git operation exceeds it, it returns None, which may be silently treated as an empty result.

The `_int_arg` function silently falls back on malformed input, which is deliberate but could hide configuration errors; the docstring claims the value is echoed in the report, which cannot be verified here.
